nodeTypes.label: Frontend / Client
nodeTypes.description: What users see and interact with — the browser, mobile app, or any screen where someone uses the product
nodeTypes.analogy: The storefront window and counters of a business. Everything the customer touches and sees.

nodeTypes.label: Server
nodeTypes.description: The backend that does the thinking — receives requests, runs business logic, and coordinates other components
nodeTypes.analogy: The back office of a restaurant. Customers never see it, but every order flows through here.

nodeTypes.label: Database
nodeTypes.description: Where your data lives permanently — the system of record that remembers everything even after restarts
nodeTypes.analogy: The filing cabinet that stores all your important records. Slower to access than your desk, but nothing gets lost.

nodeTypes.label: Cache
nodeTypes.description: A fast, temporary storage layer that keeps frequently accessed data close at hand to avoid slow database lookups
nodeTypes.analogy: A cookbook on the kitchen counter instead of in the bookshelf. Limited space, but anything there is instant to grab.

nodeTypes.label: Message Queue
nodeTypes.description: A waiting line for tasks — lets one part of the system hand off work to another without waiting for it to finish
nodeTypes.analogy: A ticket counter where you drop off your request and get a number. You don't have to stand there while they process it.

nodeTypes.label: Load Balancer
nodeTypes.description: A traffic director that spreads incoming requests evenly across multiple servers so no single one gets overwhelmed
nodeTypes.analogy: A host at a restaurant who seats guests at different tables to keep every section equally busy.

nodeTypes.label: CDN (Content Delivery Network)
nodeTypes.description: A global network of servers that stores copies of your static files (images, scripts) close to users around the world
nodeTypes.analogy: Having branch offices in every city instead of one headquarters — customers get what they need from the nearest location.

nodeTypes.label: API Gateway
nodeTypes.description: The single front door that receives all incoming requests and routes them to the right backend service
nodeTypes.analogy: The front desk at a hotel. Every guest request goes through the front desk, which figures out who to call.

nodeTypes.label: Authentication
nodeTypes.description: How the system verifies who you are and what you're allowed to do
nodeTypes.analogy: The security guard at the building entrance who checks your ID badge and makes sure you only go to floors you have access to.

nodeTypes.label: External Service
nodeTypes.description: A third-party service your system depends on — payment processors, email providers, AI APIs, analytics
nodeTypes.analogy: Suppliers and contractors your business relies on. You don't make everything in-house — you outsource to specialists.

nodeTypes.label: Background Job
nodeTypes.description: Tasks that run behind the scenes without making the user wait — sending emails, processing images, syncing data
nodeTypes.analogy: The back office that handles paperwork after the customer leaves. The customer doesn't wait while their receipt is filed.

nodeTypes.label: File Storage
nodeTypes.description: Where files, images, documents, and uploads are kept — separate from the database, optimized for large binary data
nodeTypes.analogy: The warehouse where you store physical inventory. Different from the office filing cabinet (database) — this is for bulky items.

nodeTypes.label: AI Agent
nodeTypes.description: An autonomous AI component that can reason, make decisions, and take actions — often orchestrating calls to LLMs and tools
nodeTypes.analogy: A skilled assistant who can figure out what needs to happen and do it, rather than just following a fixed script.
